**Directions: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank in the given sentence. **

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'everyday'.

__
 
• Let us explore the given options__:

 __
 
• The adjective 'future' means **the events that will or are likely to happen in time to come**.
 
• The adjective 'everyday' means **happening or used every day; daily**.
 
• The adjective '**average**' means **constituting the result obtained by adding together several amounts and then dividing this total by the number of amounts**.
 
• The adjective 'habitual' means **done constantly or as a habit**.
 
 

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

Complete Sentence__: *We must not take the future for granted; rather, we should enjoy the **everyday** joys of our humdrum lives*.

questions.question:
**Directions: Identify the segment in the given sentence which contains the grammatical error. **

Soni take her daughter to the park in the evening in a stroller.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Soni take her daughter**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the use of the plural form of the verb 'take' is incorrect.
 
• The noun 'Soni' in the given sentence is **a singular subject**.
 
• We know that **a singular subject will always take a singular verb**.
 
• Therefore, the **singular form of the verb 'takes'** should be used **in place of 'take'**.

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Correct Sentence__: ***Soni takes her daughter** to the park in the evening in a stroller*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Subjects and verbs must agree with one another in number (singular or plural).
 
• Thus, if a subject is singular, its verb must also be singular; if a subject is plural, its verb must also be plural.

questions.question:
**Directions: Select the option that is the passive form of the given sentence. **

This book explores the secret of leading a long and meaningful life.

options.text: The secret of leading a long and meaningful life was being explored by this book.
The secret of leading a long and meaningful life is explored in this book.
The secret of leading a long and meaningful life had been explored by this book.
The secret of leading a long and meaningful life have been explored by this book.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**The secret of leading a long and meaningful life is explored in this book**.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/64e177b3c5c5cb81c12b3d5b5ddabaaf474cdad3d6098992ca6592786c8147d6.png] 

 
• In **Active Voice**, a sentence emphasizes the subject, performing an action.
 
• In **Passive Voice**, a sentence emphasizes the action or the object of the sentence.
 
• The **given sentence** is in the **active voice** and '**This book**' is the **subject **and '**the secret of leading a long and meaningful life**' is the **object.**
 
• When we convert this sentence into **passive voice**, the subject '**This book**' of the **active voice** becomes the** object**, the **object **'**the secret of leading a long and meaningful life**' becomes the **subject**.
 
• The passive format "**is + V3 (explored)**" should be used.
 
• This is the active and passive voice **rule** for the **present simple tense**.

Hence, the correct answer is** option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/87c1a28e731fadd9279228c1cea2f8e988a3f790bf9ccc89c9b0f02c423b1609.png]

questions.question:
**Directions: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order. **

A. The father then wanted his son to pick him up at four in the afternoon so that they could go home together.

B. A teenager had just passed his driving test and was eager to drive his father’s car.

C. He asked his son to drop him at a place that was some 18 miles from home before he took the car for servicing.

D. His father agreed.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "BDCA".

​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence 'B' is independent of any other sentences as it is giving general information about **"**A teenager". Hence, 'B' is the first part.
 
• The noun "father" mentioned in the sentence 'D' refers back to the 'father' mentioned in the sentence 'B'. Hence, 'D' follows 'B'.
 
• The pronoun "He" mentioned in the sentence 'C' refers back to the noun "father" in the sentence 'D'. Hence, 'C' follows 'D'.
 
• The sentence 'A' is the concluding sentence. Hence, the sentence 'A' is the last sentence.

 

After rearranging the sentences__: *A teenager had just passed his driving test and was eager to drive his father’s car. His father agreed. He asked his son to drop him at a place that was some 18 miles from home before he took the car for servicing. The father then wanted his son to pick him up at four in the afternoon so that they could go home together*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__** 

__
 
• Important Rules to Solve the Para Jumbles__:

 
 
• Read the sentences attentively and try to comprehend the idea or theme of the sentence and eliminate the irrelevant options.
 
• Try to identify the opening (independent sentence) and closing sentences (concluding sentence).
 
• Try to identify the mandatory pairs. Two sentences can be connected through various connectors and other determinants.

questions.question:
**Directions: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order. **

A. In reality, however, we exist in compartments, separated by walls of caste, religion, and geography.

B. But we find that ignorance levels are growing as well because the rate at which we are accumulating information is not commensurate with the rate at which our awareness is growing.

C. Technologically we live in a borderless world.

D. Another paradox is that we take pride in describing ourselves as a knowledge-based society.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "CADB".**
​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence 'C' is independent of any other sentences as it is giving general information about a "borderless world". Hence, 'C' is the first part.
 
• The use of the adverb "however" in the sentence 'A' indicates that** it contrasts with or seems to contradict something that has been said previously in the sentence 'C'. Hence, 'A' follows 'C'.
 
• The phrase "Another paradox" mentioned in the sentence 'D' is linked with the sentence 'D'. Hence, 'D' follows 'A'.
 
• The sentence 'B' is the concluding sentence. Hence, the sentence 'B' is the last sentence.

 

After rearranging the sentences__: *Technologically we live in a borderless world. In reality, however, we exist in compartments, separated by walls of caste, religion, and geography. But we find that ignorance levels are growing as well because the rate at which we are accumulating information is not commensurate with the rate at which our awareness is growing*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **__Mistake Points__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

So to keep a stiff upper lip showed that one was unafraid and this is how the idiom came to be used in everyday language*.
